description: Only PRIJEM (positive) and VYDAJ (negative) give a signed amount; VYBER transactions are left out of the signed-amount average.

c.request: Linking each transaction to its account (skipping transactions without one), for each account statement frequency work out the average signed transaction amount — credits ('PRIJEM') positive, withdrawals negative, and any transaction that is neither left out — along with the average balance after the transaction. Then take the simple mean of those per-frequency signed averages, keep the frequencies above it, and give me one row: the average of their signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed average exceeds the mean. Don't round. Only PRIJEM (positive) and VYDAJ (negative) give a signed amount; VYBER transactions are left out of the signed-amount average.
c.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT a.frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS avg_signed, AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id GROUP BY a.frequency), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_signed) AS mean_signed FROM f) SELECT AVG(f.avg_signed) AS avg_signed_amount, AVG(f.avg_balance) AS avg_balance, AVG(f.avg_signed - m.mean_signed) AS avg_excess FROM f CROSS JOIN m WHERE f.avg_signed > m.mean_signed

b.request: For each account statement frequency (via the account linked to each transaction, skipping transactions with no account), compute the average signed transaction amount (PRIJEM positive, VYDAJ negative, VYBER and any other type excluded from this average) and the average balance after the transaction. Then take the simple mean of those per-frequency signed averages, keep only the frequencies whose signed average is above that mean, and return one row: the average of their signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed average exceeds the mean, unrounded
b.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT a.frequency AS frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type='PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type='VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS signed_avg, AVG(t.balance) AS bal_avg FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id GROUP BY a.frequency), m AS (SELECT AVG(signed_avg) AS mean_signed FROM f) SELECT AVG(f.signed_avg) AS avg_signed_avg, AVG(f.bal_avg) AS avg_balance_avg, AVG(f.signed_avg - m.mean_signed) AS avg_excess FROM f CROSS JOIN m WHERE f.signed_avg > m.mean_signed

a.request: Joining each transaction to its account (dropping transactions with no matching account), compute for each account statement frequency (`account.frequency`) the average signed transaction amount — `trans.amount` taken as positive when `trans.type` is 'PRIJEM', negative when it is 'VYDAJ', and left out (no value) for every other type, including 'VYBER' — and the average `trans.balance` over all its transactions. Then take the plain mean of those per-frequency average signed amounts, keep only the frequencies whose average signed amount is above that mean, and return a single row with: the average of their average signed amounts, the average of their average balances, and the average of how far their average signed amount exceeds the mean. Don't round.
a.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT a.frequency AS frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS avg_signed, AVG(t.balance) AS avg_balance FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id GROUP BY a.frequency), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_signed) AS mean_signed FROM f) SELECT AVG(f.avg_signed) AS avg_signed_amount, AVG(f.avg_balance) AS avg_balance, AVG(f.avg_signed - m.mean_signed) AS avg_excess FROM f CROSS JOIN m WHERE f.avg_signed > m.mean_signed

d.request: Linking each transaction to its account (skipping transactions without one), for each account statement frequency, work out the average signed transaction amount, where credits ('PRIJEM') are positive, withdrawals ('VYDAJ') are negative, and any other transaction type (including 'VYBER') is left out of the signed-amount average, along with the average balance after the transaction. Then take the simple mean of those per-frequency signed averages, keep the frequencies whose signed average is above that mean, and give me one row: the average of their signed averages, the average of their balance averages, and the average amount by which their signed average exceeds the mean. Don't round.
d.sql: WITH f AS (SELECT a.frequency, AVG(CASE WHEN t.type = 'PRIJEM' THEN t.amount WHEN t.type = 'VYDAJ' THEN -t.amount END) AS s, AVG(t.balance) AS b FROM trans t JOIN account a ON a.account_id = t.account_id GROUP BY a.frequency), m AS (SELECT AVG(s) AS ms FROM f) SELECT AVG(f.s) AS avg_signed_avg, AVG(f.b) AS avg_balance_avg, AVG(f.s - m.ms) AS avg_excess FROM f CROSS JOIN m WHERE f.s > m.ms
